title: Split ephemeral vs persistent Terraform surface and migrate legacy LB/state
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Long plan/apply times and frequent drift in networking changes are slowing platform launches. A lot of churn is caused by Terraform touching long-lived resources (NATs, EIPs, load balancers) during short-lived environment updates. Multiple teams have hacked around this by creating ephemeral overlays which are not well-structured; state is scattered across workspaces and some legacy LB resources were manually provisioned and are outside IaC.

Goal: Refactor IaC surface to explicitly separate ephemeral (short-lived) resources from persistent networking primitives, standardize module interfaces, and perform a safe state migration/import of legacy ALB/NLB objects into dedicated persistent state workspaces. This should reduce terraform plan/apply walltimes for dev/staging by >40%, simplify drift investigations, and make environment tear-downs safe.

Scope:
- Introduce two top-level module faces: network-persistent (VPC, subnets, route tables, NAT gateways, ALBs/NLBs, EIP allocations) and network-ephemeral (load-balancer listeners for ephemeral test clusters, ephemeral route overrides, ephemeral security group rules).
- Create a migration harness that imports legacy load balancer and EIP resources into network-persistent state, and records mapping metadata.
- Consolidate provider versions and upgrade to Terraform 1.8-compatible module patterns; bump aws provider to 5.x and pin in root modules.
- Add terraform CI gates to run a fast graph/planner job and reject PRs that touch persistent state without an owner approval label.
- Add module contract tests (unit-style) using terratest/ktest harness for common invariants (tagging, lifecycle rules, immutable attributes).

Non-goals: Changing networking architecture (no CIDR reworks), migrating cloud accounts, or changing production routing policies in this ticket.

Acceptance criteria:
- network-persistent and network-ephemeral modules exist in the repo with clear input/output contracts and examples.
- Legacy ALB/NLB/EIP resources for envs: staging-us-west-2 and ci-us-east-1 are imported into persistent state with documented mapping.
- CI job reduces full-plan runs for ephemeral PRs by routing them to ephemeral-only plans and completes within target time.
- Performance: plan time for ephemeral-only changes reduced by >=40% in sampled PRs.

Migration plan (high-level):
1) Audit: inventory current resources and manual LBs (confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/infra/networking/legacy-lb-audit).
2) Create persistent module and test import in sandbox account (sandbox: account-qa-19).
3) Run import/migrate with maintenance window and create migration PRs. Each import step will have an approval checklist.
4) Converge; run acceptability tests and smoke tests (routing, healthchecks) in staging.
5) Rollout: update downstream overlays to reference new module outputs.

Rollback: If import causes unexpected disruption, we have the following rollback plan: revert IaC changes, re-attach resources to legacy state (we keep backup state copies), and open incident channel. Detailed rollback runbook is attached in the migration doc.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: accidental replacement of resources during import. Mitigation: dry-run imports in sandbox, manual state takeovers with -target and import state backups.
- Risk: CI rejects legitimate changes. Mitigation: add temporary bypass label with auditor sign-off and monitor for false positives.

References:
- GH draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4822 (WIP)
- Confluence migration spec: https://confluence.redwood.ai/infra/networking/ephemeral-persistent-modules
- Dashboard (apply times): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/infra/terraform-plan-duration
